I'm 73 years old, been farming these fields for 50 years. Me and the old lady, just us two now. We got 5.5 mu total — not much land, but it's ours. I keep 2.5 mu in cotton for the cash income, and 3 mu in stevia. I shifted more to stevia these past few years because my back can't take all that cotton picking anymore, and stevia comes back every spring on its own. We don't have much cash to throw around, so I have to think careful about every yuan.

For the cotton, I'll plant around April 22nd, when the apricot trees start blooming — that's my calendar, don't need no almanac. I'm using the same seed as last year, saved some from my own crop and bought a little from my nephew to top up. Before planting I spread about half a bag of compound fertilizer per mu, around 25 kg. Then when the cotton starts flowering in June, I topdress with another half bag of urea, maybe 15 kg. I know Old Wang down the road uses more, but fertilizer got expensive last year and I can't put everything into the cotton — the stevia needs some too. Better to put a bit extra than too little though, because if the yield drops, that's worse than wasting a little fertilizer. I'll water it twice — once in late June when it's hot and the flowers are opening, and once in August when the bolls are filling. Each pumping costs me about 30-40 yuan but without it the cotton won't fill properly and then the year's work is wasted. I spray herbicide once after planting and insecticide twice for bollworm — that pest never gives up. Me and the old lady do most of the work, but during picking season in September and October I hire Old Zhang's daughter for 5 days — her hands are fast and my back can't handle bending over 2.5 mu of cotton for weeks. Last year I got about 260 kg of lint per mu, and if the weather holds I hope for the same.

For the stevia, it's already in the ground from last year, wakes up in April when the soil warms. I spread some farmyard manure and about 20 kg of compound fertilizer per mu when I see the new shoots coming. First cut is in July, second in August, and if the frost holds off maybe a third in September. After each cut I give it a little urea, about 5 kg per mu, to help it grow back strong. Water it twice — once in May if it's dry, and once in July after the first cut. The stevia has its own smell that keeps some bugs away, so I only spray herbicide once in spring, no insecticide needed. The old lady and me manage the stevia ourselves, no hired labor — we can cut it with a sickle sitting on a low stool. Last year got about 200 kg dry leaves per mu, hope for the same this year.

All together, seed for cotton about 40 yuan per mu, fertilizer about 180 yuan per mu for cotton and 120 yuan for stevia, pesticide about 80 yuan for cotton and 20 for stevia, pumping about 60 yuan per mu, and hired labor 5 days at 100 yuan. Total comes to about 1,750 yuan. That's about my limit — can't borrow more at my age, the bank won't lend to an old man, so if something breaks I need cash in my pocket.
